t: This is the site of the former Elizabeth Garrett Anderson and Obstetric Hospital in Bloomsbury, which gave health care to women in central London from the mid-Victorian era. It is named after Elizabeth Garrett Anderson, the first woman to qualify in Britain as a physician and surgeon, and a co-founder of the London School of Medicine for Women. Its work carries on in the Elizabeth Garrett Anderson wing of University College Hospital. The suffragettes Vera Wentworth and Aeta Adelaide Lamb died here, as did the surgeon Maud Chadburn, and the wildlife painter Brian Cutmore was born here.
